title: Change of rings between quasi-coherent algebras: quasi-coherence and affine sections
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal B$ and $\mathcal C$ be sheaves of commutative $\mathcal O_Y$-algebras whose underlying $\mathcal O_Y$-modules are quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent], let $\varphi:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ be a morphism of sheaves of $\mathcal O_Y$-algebras, and let $\mathcal P$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal B$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] whose underlying $\mathcal O_Y$-module (through $\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal B$) is quasi-coherent. Let $\mathcal P\otimes_{\mathcal B}\mathcal C$ be the change of rings along $\varphi$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], the sheafification of the presheaf $W\mapsto\mathcal P(W)\otimes_{\mathcal B(W)}\mathcal C(W)$, a sheaf of $\mathcal C$-modules, and let $t_W:\mathcal P(W)\otimes_{\mathcal B(W)}\mathcal C(W)\to(\mathcal P\otimes_{\mathcal B}\mathcal C)(W)$ be the component of the sheafification map. Then the underlying $\mathcal O_Y$-module of $\mathcal P\otimes_{\mathcal B}\mathcal C$ (through $\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$) is quasi-coherent, and for every affine open $W\subseteq Y$ the map $t_W$ is bijective.

proof.text: Put P_0 equal to P restricted to O_Y and S=C_0 tensor_O P_0. Apply the tensor-product affine-sections theorem first to C_0,P_0 and then to B_0,S. Thus S and F=B_0 tensor_O S are quasi-coherent and both section tensor maps are bijective on affine opens.
The tensor relation presentation supplies δ:F->S, the isomorphism e from underlying change of rings to coker δ, and the pure tensor relation and comparison formulas.

Apply quasiCoherent_cokernel_image to δ: its cokernel is quasi-coherent; on every affine open its projection is surjective with kernel range δ_W. Transfer quasi-coherence to change of rings along e inverse.

For affine W, the two section tensor bijections and the section cokernel formula meet exactly the hypotheses of tensor_relation_section_quotient. Obtain the additive equivalence λ with λ(c tensor_B p)=q_W(τ(c,p)).

The comparison formula for e and the pure tensor formula for λ give e_W(η_W(z))=λ(z) by TensorProduct.induction_on (zero, pure tensor, add). Since λ and e_W are bijective, η_W is injective (apply injectivity of the composite) and surjective (lift e_W(y) through the composite and cancel e_W). This is the original affine-section conclusion.
